abstract.text: A small HTTP/1.1 server for apps and tools: routing, files, forms, uploads and WebSockets, without dependencies.

inlineContent.text: NanoHTTP runs a web server inside your process: a command-line tool, a Mac app or an iOS app. You register
functions for methods and paths, and the framework takes care of sockets, threads and the protocol.
Pages are built with the companion library NanoHTML (a second product of the package), which escapes text for you.
It is meant for servers that are used by you, your own devices or a small trusted group: tools, local
user interfaces, companion apps, test servers. It does not provide TLS, authentication or protection against
says what to take care of.

An HTTP request: method, path, query, headers and body, plus the address of the client and the
variables of the route that matched. The server creates one for every request and hands it to
middleware and handlers. A request is a reference type, compared and hashed by identity.
A function that answers a request. It runs on the thread of the connection that sent the request,
one request at a time per connection, and many handlers run at the same time for different
connections (unless the server has only one thread). A handler may block (a slow handler delays only
its own connection) but must protect state that it shares with other handlers.
